name: tellegen-workspace
description: JavaScript workspace for the tellegen browser packages, hosted demo, and examples.

scripts.build:example: npm run build:example:browser && npm run build:example:svelte
scripts.check:web: npm run build:webmcp && npm run build:svelte && npm --workspace tellegen-frontend run check
scripts.build:web: npm run build:webmcp && npm run build:svelte && npm --workspace tellegen-frontend run build
scripts.check: npm run check:engine && npm run check:webmcp && npm run check:svelte && npm run check:web
scripts.build: npm run build:engine && npm run build:webmcp && npm run build:svelte && npm run build:example && npm --workspace tellegen-frontend run build
scripts.test:downstream: npm run test:import && npm run test:svelte-packed
scripts.ci:js: npm run check && npm run build && npm run pack:webmcp && npm run pack:svelte && npm run smoke:web && npm run test:downstream && npm run test:evidence
scripts.version:packages: changeset version && npm run contracts && npm install --package-lock-only --ignore-scripts

//overrides: Vite must be a single copy. @sveltejs/kit and vite-plugin-svelte import `vite` at runtime for its resolve defaults, and vitest pulls its own; a workspace on a different major than the hoisted one is an npm-resolution accident waiting to bite. The `$vite` alias resolves to the range declared above, which is why vite is also a root dependency, and it keeps Dependabot in charge of the version.
